factProposals.value: The system is deployed on-premises with `npm run deploy`, which opens the SQLite database, starts the HTTP server and checks /api/health and the asset records before declaring the deployment done.
The server uses Node 24 built-ins only (node:http, node:sqlite, node:test); there are no third-party packages to install.
Asset records are created and read over HTTP, are idempotent by asset tag, and every change is written to an append-only audit trail.

decisions.statement: A deployment only counts once a system.deploy audit event (version, commit, host, database, checks, duration) has been written.
decisions.rationale: the story's trust criterion makes the audit entry part of the deployment

decisions.statement: A failed deployment stops the server and is audited as system.deploy_failed where the database allows.
decisions.rationale: a half-started system must not keep serving

decisions.statement: Core functionalities for the first deployment are the health check and asset records.
decisions.rationale: agreed with the student as the thinnest end-to-end path

limitations.statement: Active Directory sign-in and two-factor (REQ-010) were not part of this story; sign-in was a development stand-in until STORY-012.
Near-real-time replication (an option in REQ-002) is not built; backups are the only protection.
